item.title: US-Israeli war created 'horrific' situation for Iranians: Amnesty
item.description:
Iranian authorities have intensified their repression of the country's population in response to the Middle East war, which began weeks after their deadly crackdown on anti-government protests killed thousands of people, Amnesty International said on Tuesday.

An internet blackout imposed at the time of the crackdown on January 8 and 9 and the scale of the casualties meant it was not yet possible for the group to quantify the number of people killed, Amnesty's lead Iran researcher, Raha Bahreini, said.

item.title: UK sanctions Israeli firms helping build West Bank settlements
item.description:
Britain announced Tuesday a slew of sanctions against eight Israeli companies helping to plan and build West Bank settlements, in its latest curbs on individuals and organisations in Israel connected to settler activity.

The new measures -- aimed at hindering expansion of the settlements, which are considered illegal under international law -- also follow what the UK government has called a reset of its approach to the issue in September.

item.title: Trump and Tehran gamble on time as Iran war stalemate deepens
item.description:
By Samia Nakhoul and John Irish

DUBAI/PARIS, Nov 17 (Reuters) - After nearly nine months of war, the United States and Iran are each acting as if they have time on their side, a calculation that has locked them in a stalemate that is almost impossible for either to break.

It is a risky gamble, with two former US Middle East negotiators, European officials and Gulf sources saying fighting could resume before a diplomatic exit becomes possible.

item.title: UN agency warns of Gaza hypothermia deaths without more supplies
item.description:
By Emma Farge

GENEVA, Nov 17 (Reuters) - The UN migration agency warned on Tuesday of further deaths from hypothermia in Gaza and called for more funding and shelter supplies ahead of winter after a baby died from cold.

Heavy rain has already flooded tens of thousands of tents housing displaced Palestinians crammed into encampments after the war between Israel and Hamas reduced much of the Gaza Strip to rubble. Last week, a 9-month-old baby living in a tent died from suspected hypothermia, UN agencies and Gaza authorities said, andrespiratory illnesses are rising.

item.title: Saudi Arabia defends stance on climate reports amid COP31 fight
item.description:
Saudi Arabia on Tuesday defended its position over the publication timeline of crucial reports by the UN's climate science panel as a dispute over the issue heats up at the COP31 summit.

Several countries are pushing for a reference to the timing standoff to be included in a broad political statement being negotiated at the UN's climate talks in Antalya, Turkey.

item.title: Quad leaders flag 'economic coercion', oppose unilateral actions undermining peace
item.description:
NEW DELHI, Nov 17 (Reuters) - Leaders of the four-nation Quad grouping strongly oppose any destabilising or unilateral actions that seek to change the status quo, including by force or coercion, which escalate tensions and undermine regional peace and stability, a joint statement said on Tuesday.

The leaders also expressed grave concerns about economic coercion, including through arbitrary export restrictions, the statement added after their meeting in Manila.

(Reporting by Hritam Mukherjee and Tanvi Mehta; Editing by YP Rajesh)

item.title: Trump says US taking seriously report of possible Iranian dirty bomb plot in Washington
item.description:
DUBAI, Nov 17 (Reuters) - President Donald Trump said on Tuesday the US was taking seriously the possibility that Iran could be planning an attack involving a so-called dirty bomb in Washington, after being asked about a CNN report citing USintelligence assessments.

Trump nodded when asked by a reporter whether Iran was planning to detonate a dirty bomb in the UScapital.

"We're looking into it," Trump told reporters during a photo opportunity in Manila.

item.title: Iraqi leader's planned crackdown on pro-Iran militias is riskiest move yet
item.description:
By Ahmed Rasheed and Michael Georgy

BAGHDAD/DUBAI Nov 17 (Reuters) - Just six months after coming to power as a political novice, Iraq's Prime Minister Alial-Zaidi is planning his riskiest move yet: directly confronting the heavily armed Shi'ite militias that function as proxies of Iran.

The 41-year-old businessman-turned-politician has told his security forces to prepare to take on Iran's most powerful ally in Iraq, Kataib Hezbollah, a group which officials have accused of running a smuggling ring that siphoned off hundreds of millions of dollars' worth of state-owned oil.

item.title: Explainer-How is genocide proven in court?
item.description:
By Stephanie van den Berg

THE HAGUE, Nov 17 (Reuters) - The United Nations' top court, the International Court of Justice, will rule on Thursday in a case in which Gambia accuses Myanmar of committing genocide against its Rohingya Muslim minority in 2017.

Genocide is notoriously difficult to prove. Here are some key points ahead of the ruling.

WHAT IS GENOCIDE?

item.title: Top UN court ruling on Myanmar genocide to be watched for clues on Gaza
item.description:
By Stephanie van den Berg and Ruma Paul

THE HAGUE/COX'S BAZAR, Bangladesh, Nov 17 (Reuters) - The United Nations' highest court is set to rule on Thursday on whether Myanmar's 2017 military campaign against the minority Rohingya amounted to genocide, in a closely watched case that could shape how courts assess state responsibility for the gravest crime under international law.

item.title: Britain sanctions Israeli settlement firms in push to protect two-state solution
item.description:
By Andrew MacAskill

LONDON, Nov 17 (Reuters) - Britain said on Tuesday it would impose sanctions on eight Israeli construction companies involved in building settlements in the occupied West Bank, as part of its effort to protect the idea of a two-state solution.

The firms targeted for asset freezes and director disqualifications include Har Hevron Development Company Ltd, Hemdat Shomron Ltd and S.A.G. (Velvel) Construction and Development Ltd, which build and develop homes in the West Bank.

item.title: Israeli settlers kill Palestinian woman, 72, in West Bank
item.description:
By Pesha Magid and Ali Sawafta

JERICHO, West Bank, Nov 17 (Reuters) - Israeli militant settlers shot dead a 72-year-old Palestinian woman overnight in a part of the occupied West Bank city of Jericho where settlers recently took over several Palestinian homes, witnesses and Palestinian officials said.

The Israeli military did not comment on the woman's death but did describe "ongoing incidents" with Palestinians and Israelis injured in an alleged Palestinian car-ramming.
